The documented SNS grant baseline replayed, and the fresh-topic/fresh-key case replayed despite an explicit unconditional sns.amazonaws.com kms:Decrypt Deny present before the first publication. The owner/publisher grant remained unchanged.
Both original messages replayed into new queues at approximately eight minutes while the explicit SNS Decrypt Deny was present. These receipts do not establish a cold archive authorization decision.

At approximately twenty minutes, with both original keys disabled and the explicit SNS Decrypt Deny still present, neither fresh queue received its original message during its recorded approximately 83-second receive window. Both subscriptions reported the native ReplayStatus value Completed, not Failed.

After enabling the same original keys and removing only the explicit SNS Deny, new subscriptions/queues received the exact original MessageIds and message bodies, with Replayed=true. These were new replay requests, not a demonstrated retry or repair of the earlier Completed subscriptions.

The supplemental EventName=Decrypt CloudTrail lookup captured real successful AWSService / sns.amazonaws.com Decrypt calls at 2026-09-23T01:17:49Z and 2026-09-23T01:17:57Z, using the respective original key ARNs and exact topic encryption contexts. These coincide with the restored replay receipts. This is direct evidence of an actual archive KMS decrypt decision, not an inference from elapsed idle time.

Publication-time GenerateDataKey and Decrypt calls instead identify IAMUser arn:aws:iam::000000000000:user/Delegated, invokedBy sns.amazonaws.com. The final captured owned-key event set contains two GenerateDataKey calls and four Decrypt calls: two publisher Decrypt calls and two later SNS AWSService Decrypt calls.

No failed owned-key Decrypt event was returned by the captured lookups. The disabled-key and explicit-Deny conditions were combined at twenty minutes, so the bounded absence cannot independently establish which condition prevented those receipts.
conclusions.actionable_production_implication: Keep publisher/live retained-key authorization distinct from archive replay authorization: actual cold archive Decrypt calls use the SNS service identity and the original historical key/topic context. Preserve archived entries so a later fresh replay after key/policy restoration can deliver the original message. Do not force immediate denial on every replay, claim a five-minute archive cache TTL, or report Failed merely because an unreadable archived message yields no receipt; the observed no-receipt replay status was Completed. The documentation specifies service-principal permissions; this capture directly confirms that principal on successful cold use but does not isolate an explicit-Deny-only cold failure.
limits: The eight-minute success and twenty-minute bounded absence do not measure an exact cache lifetime or prove the cache stores plaintext versus decrypted data keys.
No enabled-key, explicit-SNS-Deny-only cold replay was isolated. Disable/enable and Deny removal were combined before the successful cold replay, so no separate denial/repair causality is claimed.

ResourceName=key ARN lookups returned GenerateDataKey and management events but omitted Decrypt events subsequently found by EventName. The supplemental EventName lookups preserve each selected owned event unchanged apart from credential-identifier redaction and JSON reserialization, and explicitly report omitted unrelated-event counts.

The KMS CloudTrail guide states cross-account access-denied requests are logged only in the caller account. Together with propagation and selector limitations, this prevents treating missing failed events in the owning account as proof that no denied service call occurred.

No claim is made that Completed implies successful delivery, that the earlier Completed subscriptions later repaired themselves, or that the approximately 83-second windows are a universal failure timeout.
No key rotation, alias retargeting, archive segment eviction mechanism or region/account variation was exercised.

documented_contract: The topic-owner guide requires an SNS service-principal kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey Allow on the historical key, retaining existing grants; disabled/deleted keys or incorrectly configured policy prevent replay.
experiment_design: Two isolated encrypted FIFO archives: documented Allow baseline, and fresh topic/key with explicit unconditional sns.amazonaws.com kms:Decrypt Deny before first publication. Owner/publisher root grant always intact. Fresh standard SQS queues avoid FIFO deduplication. Observe warm and eight-minute denied replays, disable original keys until twenty-minute replay, restore keys/grants and replay original publication, then collect propagated CloudTrail. Elapsed time alone never establishes a cache miss.
limitations: A receive-window absence is not a native Failed status or universal timeout.
Fresh queues and subscriptions do not establish a fresh SNS archive cache.
CloudTrail event history is eventually consistent; event absence does not prove no KMS call.
No functions, roles or log groups are created; only topics, subscriptions, queues and two customer-managed keys.
Customer-managed keys remain PendingDeletion for the native minimum seven-day window.
